_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 11: Boombox (id 'boombox')
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote; DERIVED = arithmetic done here; EFFECTIVE = fitted (red lambda_c only); INFERRED = a reading not stated; MEASURED = read from Fig. 1 with its 200 mm scale bar.

P26.cite: Piotrowski, J. J., Frostig, D., Mueller, M., et al. 2026, "Optical design of Boombox: a high-throughput optical spectrograph on dual-hemisphere 6.5-meter telescopes", SUBMITTED SPIE paper (Ground-based and Airborne Instrumentation for Astronomy XI), manuscript dated 2026-07-19, 9 pp. NOT YET PUBLISHED: quotes are kept short
P26.url: (none: manuscript supplied by the Via team; Figs. 1-2 and 4 are raster images, so figure labels are not machine-checkable)

VO.cite: The Via Collaboration 2026, "The Via Project: Overview of the Science, Instrument, and Survey", arXiv:2606.18332 (the earlier source for the 36 fibers, bands 3600-5900 / 5700-10100 and the 2048 x 256 CCD). Sec. 2.4, Figs. 13, 15, 16

parameters.value: 6.5 m MMT and Magellan Clay (one Boombox on each)
parameters.quote: 6.5-m MMT & Magellan Clay
parameters.note: "Two Boombox spectrographs, one for each telescope" (Sec. 3.3, p. 9) [checked below]. Boombox drives the pointing 10% of the 500-night survey.

parameters.quote: 36 dedicated optical fibers

alt.quote: accepting 36 fibers from the focal plane

parameters.note: of the 636 the Via fiber positioning system routes; no sky or calibration fibers are counted in the paper's 36 (nObj 36 stays).

parameters.quote: Fiber core diameter 200 µm (1.2′′ on-sky)
parameters.note: unmasked (no slit mask) in the older sources.

parameters.quote: 1.2′′ on-sky
collimating the f/5.3 output of the fibers into a 50 mm diameter beam
parameters.note: the old preset used f/5.2 (measured from a Zemax drawing).

parameters.parameter: Telescope focal ratio into the fibers (explorer F)
parameters.quote: Fiber core diameter 200 µm
parameters.note: NOT stated. 200 um = 1.2 arcsec on 6.5 m gives F = 0.2 mm / (1.2/206265 x 6500 mm) = 5.29, equal to the f/5.3 fiber output (no focal-ratio degradation claimed). The preset uses F = f_col/W = 264/50 = 5.28, which keeps the collimator at exactly 264 mm and the slit at 1.202 arcsec (full core). Plate scale 200 um / 1.2 arcsec = 167 um/arcsec (DERIVED).

parameters.quote: The fiber slit length is 13.6 mm

alt.quote: the 13.6 mm slit length

parameters.note: 36 fibers; pitch (13.6 - 0.2)/35 = 0.383 mm if 13.6 mm is the outer extent (DERIVED, INFERRED reading), a gap of 0.18 mm, matching the quoted 'about 200 um'.

parameters.parameter: Gap between fibers on the slit
parameters.quote: A non-illuminated gap is left between each fiber of about 200 µm
parameters.note: on the chip: fiber image 200 x 0.284 = 56.8 um = 3.8 px; pitch 0.383 x 0.284 = 109 um = 7.3 px (DERIVED); the as-built EE95 limit 24.6 um is 'half the gap between spectra' (Sec. 3), so the gap is 49.2 um (consistent with 109 - 56.8 = 52 um).

parameters.quote: the system magnification (collimator and camera) is 0.28×
parameters.note: 75/264 = 0.284 (DERIVED check).

parameters.parameter: Spectra on the detector, chip height
parameters.quote: squeezes 36 spectra onto a compact detector (3.95 mm tall)
parameters.note: 263 rows x 15 um = 3.945 mm.

layout.measurement: Fig. 1 (left, p. 3) carries a 200 mm scale bar: 431.7 px between the end-cap centers of the embedded 3807 x 1735 px image = 2.158 px/mm. Checks: the drawn slit tick is 28 px = 13.0 mm (text: 13.6 mm); the five collimated rays span 111 px = 51 mm (text: 50 mm). Scale uncertainty about 3%, positions about +-3 mm.

layout.item: Order of elements (Fig. 1, top view, one on-axis field point)
layout.measurement: fiber slit -> collimator triplet (CL1 CaF2, CL2 BSM51Y, CL3 S-FPL55) -> dichroic -> [blue: reflected down-left to the blue grating -> blue camera (axis horizontal, detector at the far left)] / [red: transmitted straight to a 45 deg fold mirror that turns it down -> red grating -> red camera (axis down-left, detector at the bottom)].
layout.evidence: Fig. 1 caption: Light is injected into the instrument at the fiber slit, split in wavelength at the dichroic beamsplitter, dispersed by the transmission grating, and imaged by each camera lens

layout.measurement: slit to the first lens (CL1 front vertex) 252 mm; the triplet is 81 mm long (CL1 front to CL3 back); slit to the last vertex 333 mm. Fig. 2 (p. 4, own 100 mm scale bar) shows the f/5.3 cone and the 300 mm pupil relief.
the slit is perpendicular to the page in Fig. 1 (Via overview Fig. 15 caption: 'The fiber slit is defined perpendicular to the page'); spectra run along the dispersion in the page plane.

CL3 last vertex to the dichroic center 113 mm; dichroic to the BLUE grating center 214 mm (path 328 mm from the vertex); dichroic to the fold mirror 66 mm and fold to the RED grating 129 mm (path 309 mm). The text's 300 mm pupil relief is measured from the lens assembly: the drawn paths run 3-9% longer (scale uncertainty and the Fig. 1 prescription predates the glass substitution). Preset: layLen = 300 + 40 (half the triplet) = 340 mm (DERIVED), both arms.

plate line at 68.6 deg to the beam axis (AOI 21.4 deg); blue beam leaves at 137.25 deg to the incoming beam (Hough fit of 4 rays), the red continues straight. Preset blue foldAng = 360 - (180 - 2 x 22) = 224 deg (the old one was 225), foldPos 0.45 = (40 + 113)/340 (DERIVED).
flat at 45 deg turning the red beam 90 deg to the SAME side as the blue (both turn clockwise on the page), 66 mm past the dichroic; foldAng 270, foldPos 0.65 = (40 + 113 + 66)/340 (the old 0.64).

substrate faces 65.1 deg to the page's horizontal; beam incidence alpha = 17.9 deg (beam at 42.75 deg below horizontal, normal at 24.9 deg); camera axis horizontal, so diffraction beta = 24.9 deg on the other side of the normal; camera-collimator angle (alpha + beta, the explorer's psi) = 42.8 deg. First order: lambda at the camera axis = (sin 17.9 + sin 24.9)/1.516 = 4800 A (INFERRED). +-0.5 deg.

substrate faces 16.5 deg to the page's horizontal; the beam arrives vertically, so alpha = 16.5 deg; the detector center lies 332 mm along a line 37 deg from the incoming beam (the detector plane is perpendicular to it within 0.6 deg), so beta = 20.5 deg and psi = 37.1 deg (+-1 deg); lambda at the camera axis = (sin 16.5 + sin 20.5)/0.836 = 7600 A (INFERRED). THIS DOES NOT REACH THE BAND (see the model check).

blue: grating center to the detector surface 362 mm, so camLen (the explorer's disperser-to-camera drawing distance = detector distance - f_cam) = 362 - 75 = 287 mm; red: 332 mm, camLen 257 mm. The old values were 267 and 229 (342 and 304 mm to the detector).
Fig. 4 (p. 6) shows the 6-element blue camera and the 5-element red camera, after the glass substitution; the camera lengths scale with the 75 mm focal length.

Fig. 1 (right): the opto-mechanical rendering shows the fiber input and back-illumination system on the top, the LANSIS 261 cameras on focus stages, in a pentagonal enclosure scaled to the Zemax layout.
